_readme: Reasoned exceptions for tools/chronology_audit.py.
The audit is structural-consistency-only: it flags a discovery/output that
has NO chronologically consistent recipe or producing technique at all.
Most of those flags mean the underlying data is genuinely wrong (a date or
a recipe needs a human's review) and should stay flagged, NOT be silenced
here. Only add an entry when a human has decided a specific contradiction
is not actually a mistake — for example, 'the result's date is the earliest
evidence of the general behaviour, and this one specific recipe pair is a
deliberate gameplay abstraction, not a claim about how it was first done'.
Adding an entry here NEVER changes any date, node, or recipe — it only
tells the audit to stop reporting that one already-reviewed pairing.
Schema — each entry in `exceptions`:
code:       'CH1' | 'CH2' | 'CH3'
result:     the discovery/output id (CH1/CH2: the crafted result;
CH3: the produced output)
ingredient: CH1/CH2: the later-dated ingredient id being excused;
CH3: the technique/action id being excused
reason:     REQUIRED, non-empty — why this specific pairing is not a
real contradiction. Malformed entries (no reason) are
themselves reported by the audit as CH0.
Example (illustrative only — not a real registered exception):
{ "code": "CH1", "result": "some_result", "ingredient": "some_ingredient",
"reason": "some_result's ds marks the earliest general evidence of the
behaviour; this recipe pair is a later convenience path, not the origin
claim — reviewed 2026-xx-xx." }
